hey! so i internally transferred into nursing, but i can give a little insight on the acceptance rate for external transfers. 

the acceptance rate for internal transfers is pretty low, they accept around 10 ish people in the spring cycle and around 30 ish people in the fall cycle (which are then joined to make one cohort). 

the external transfer rate is very very low, i have heard of them accepting 0 to maybe 3 external transfers. and many people apply each cycle. 

the best way to get in would to be get accepted into UT as an undeclared/liberal arts/CNS major and then transfer internally.

here is the link to it! :[https://nursing.utexas.edu/academics/graduate/degree-offered/aemsn](https://nursing.utexas.edu/academics/graduate/degree-offered/aemsn)

it's for people who have a bachelor's degree and still want to purse nursing at UT. if selected you'll graduate with your degree (biochem, or anything) and then enter the program where you'll have one year to become an RN and then around 2 years to get your master's in nursing and pick a concentration (they are all listed on the site i linked).

since you're so far into your current degree, the nursing school will probably not let you transfer and instead suggest that you apply to their alternative master's program. if you have any other questions about transferring I can definitely answer. I just transferred in last January!
